div.l: This sompnour bare to hym a styf burdoun
Was neuer trompe of half so gret a soun
This pardoner had heer as yelowe as wexe
And smothe it hynge as doth a stryke of flexe
By hounses henge his lockys that he had
And therwyth his sholders ouersprad
But then it lay by culpons one and one
An hode for Iolyte ware he none
For it was trussyd vp in his walet
Hym thoughte he rode vpon the newe get
Dyssheuylde saue his cappe he rode all bare
Suche glaryng eyen had he as hath an hare
A vernacle had he sowed vpon his cappe
His walet beforn hym had he in his lappe
Brette full of pardon come fro rome all hote
A voys he had as small as hath a gote
No berde had he ne neuer sholde haue
As smothe was it as it were newe shaue
I trowe he were a geldyng or a mare
But of his craft from berwyk vnto ware
Ne was ther nowher suche a pardoner
For in his male he had a pylow beer
Whyche as he sayd was our ladyes veyll
He sayd he had a gobet of the seyll
That saynt peter had whan that he went
Vp on the see tyll Ihesus crist hym hent
He had a crosse of laton full of stonys
And in a glas he had pygges bonys
But wᵗith thyse relyques whan that he fonde
A poore persoıı̄un dwellyng vpon londe
Vpon a daye he gate hym more moneye
Than the persoıı̄un gate in monthis tweye
And thus had he feyned flateryes ⁊and Iapis
He made the person ⁊and the peple his apis
But truely to telle at the last
He was in chyrche a noble ecclesiast
Well cowde he rede a lesson or a story
But alderbest he songe an offretory
For well he wyst whan that songe was songe
He must preche ⁊and fyle a whyle his tonge
To wynne syluer as he full well cowde
Therfore he songe the merely ⁊and lowde
Now haue I told you shortly in a clause
The state þᵉ aray the nōmbre ⁊and the cause
Why that assembled was this companye
In suthwerk at this gentyll hostelrye
That hyghte the taberd fast by the belle
But now is tyme to you for to telle
How that we bare vs that ylke nyght
Whan that we were in the hostry a lyght
And after woll I telle of our vyage
And all the remenaunt of our pylgrymage
But fyrst I you praye of your curtesye
That ye ne arette it not my vylanye
Though that I playnly speke in this matere
To tell you ther wordes ⁊and ther chere
And though I speke ther wordes properly
For this ye knowe as well as I
Who shall a tale telle after a man
He muste reherce as nere as he can
Euery worde yf it be in his charge
All speke he neuer so rudely ⁊and so large
Or ellys he must telle his tale vntrewe
Or se thynges or feyne wordes newe
He may not spare all thouȝ he were his brother
He must as well say o worde as a nother
Crist spak hymself full brode in holy wryt
And well ye wote no vylany is it
Also plato sayth who so can it rede
The worde must be cosyn to the dede
Also I praye you foryeue it me
All though I sette not folke in ther degre
Here in thyse tales as they sholde stonde
My wyt is short ye may well vnderstonde
